project: RevYield - B2B Pricing Elasticity & Revenue Optimization Engine
_readme: This is an implementation SPECIFICATION, not a Make.com blueprint export.
A blueprint export embeds account-scoped connection IDs, module UUIDs and an
internal schema version; publishing one would either leak credentials or ship a
file that silently fails to import. Every connection below is a placeholder of
the form {{CONN_*}} and must be bound in the Make UI.
Multi-line SQL and payload bodies are expressed as arrays of strings. Join with
'\n' to reconstruct. Every SQL block here parses against the PostgreSQL 16
grammar and runs against the schema in data/schema.sql.

platform_constraints._note: These are the reasons the design looks the way it does. All four tiers are free.

consequence: Polling every 15 minutes would burn 2,880 trigger operations a month before
a single deal is processed - roughly 3x the entire free allowance. Scenario 1
therefore polls hourly during business hours only, and Scenario 2 runs once
daily. Measured budget is in operations_budget below.
The HubSpot Webhooks API requires a public app in a developer account, and
workflow-triggered webhooks require Operations Hub. Neither is free. The
trigger is therefore a poll against the CRM Search API filtered on
hs_lastmodifieddate, which a free-tier private app can do.

neon_free.autosuspend: compute scales to zero when idle
consequence: The first query after idle pays a cold-start of roughly 500ms. Scenario 2
issues one query returning many rows rather than one query per account.

google_sheets.consequence: Append-only logs; rotate the exception log annually.

connections._note: Bind these in the Make UI. Never commit real IDs.

_note: HubSpot's default deal object carries dealname, amount, dealstage, pipeline,
closedate and dealtype. Everything the margin calculation needs beyond that
has to be created. POST each object below to the endpoint in
property_creation_request. 'amount' is mapped to realized_price, so no custom
property is created for it.
HubSpot deal -> fact_transactions. The warehouse column list is deliberately
short: discount_pct, gross_margin, gross_margin_pct, realized_price_per_seat,
list_price_per_seat and mrr are GENERATED columns in data/schema.sql and must
never appear in an INSERT. That is the whole point of putting them in the DDL -
Power BI, ad-hoc SQL and this pipeline cannot drift from one another.

columns.transform: toNumber - HubSpot 'amount' IS the booked ACV

deal_stage_map._note: Keys are HubSpot's default sales pipeline stage IDs.

_note: ck_txn_prob_settled in data/schema.sql requires win_probability to be exactly
1 for closed_won and exactly 0 for closed_lost. Only open deals may carry a
genuine forecast weight. These values are HubSpot's own stage defaults.

deal_type_map._note: HubSpot ships only newbusiness/existingbusiness. 'renewal' and 'upgrade' require custom options; without them the warehouse sees expansion.

_note: The database constraints ARE the integration contract. Rather than validating
in Make and hoping, the pipeline maps deliberately and lets Postgres reject
anything malformed into the error branch.
ck_txn_contract     won deals must carry both contract dates; lost and open must carry neither
ck_txn_prob_settled closed deals carry probability exactly 1 or 0
ck_txn_discount     realized_price <= list_price
ck_txn_prices       list_price > 0, realized_price > 0, unit_cost >= 0
ck_txn_seats        contracted_seats > 0
fk account_id       the company must already exist in dim_accounts
Computed in Make only to decide whether to flag the deal and what to write back
to HubSpot. They are NOT written to Neon - the generated columns recompute them
on insert. Formulas are identical to data/schema.sql by construction.

margin_floor_breach._note: Escalates regardless of headline discount. A deal can sit inside its discount band and still be below floor if the cost to serve is heavy.

scenarios.name: RevYield · Deal Margin Guard
scenarios.purpose: When a deal moves in HubSpot, price it, flag it if it breaches discount governance or the margin floor, log the exception, and keep the warehouse in step.

schedule._rationale: Hourly on business days = 12 x 22 = 264 trigger operations a month. Every 15 minutes would be 2,880 and blow the free tier on its own.

modules.label: Priceable deals only
modules._rationale: Stops half-filled deals reaching the warehouse and failing ck_txn_prices, which would push a recoverable data-entry gap into the error branch.

then.on_empty: route to error branch 'unknown_account' - never invent an account_id, the FK will reject it anyway

modules.label: Load tier economics
modules._rationale: The rate card lives in the database, so Make never carries a hard-coded price. Repricing the book means one UPDATE, not editing a scenario.

variables.approval_band: if(discount_pct <= 0.10; 'Account Executive'; if(discount_pct <= 0.20; 'Sales Manager'; if(discount_pct <= 0.30; 'VP Revenue'; 'CFO')))

modules.label: Write economics back to the deal
modules._rationale: The rep sees the approver they need before they send the quote, not after finance rejects it.

modules.label: Upsert the deal ledger
sql: account_id, deal_id, contract_tier, deal_type, deal_stage, pricing_variant,
_notes: Placeholders use PostgreSQL's native $n form, which is unambiguous about
ordering. Client libraries differ: Make's PostgreSQL module and JDBC bind an
ordered array against '?', psycopg parses '%s'. Substitute positionally to
match your module - but bind, never interpolate. dealname is free text and is
attacker-controlled in any org that accepts inbound leads.
The trailing WHERE stops a stale poll from dragging a closed-won deal back
to open. HubSpot can legitimately reopen a deal, but that should be a
deliberate correction, not a race between two scenario runs.
No generated column appears in the column list. Postgres recomputes
discount_pct, gross_margin, gross_margin_pct, realized_price_per_seat,
list_price_per_seat and mrr, which is why Make's arithmetic in module 5
can never disagree with Power BI.

operations_budget._method: Make bills one operation per module execution. Filters and routers are free. Billable per deal: 3 (associations + company lookup), 4, 5, 6, 9 = 6.

scenarios.name: RevYield · Usage Threshold Sweep
scenarios.purpose: Each morning, find accounts that have been over their contracted capacity for two consecutive months, open an expansion deal for the ones with nothing in flight, and publish the worklist.

schedule._rationale: One run per business day. The sweep reads a monthly snapshot, so anything more frequent re-reads identical data at real operational cost.

modules.label: Expansion-ready accounts
modules._note: The operational subset of sql/02_tier_expansion.sql - same thresholds, same sustained-breach rule, trimmed to what the automation acts on.
sql: SELECT MAX(recorded_date) AS d FROM fact_usage_metrics
COUNT(*)     OVER (PARTITION BY u.account_id) AS months_observed,
ORDER BY u.recorded_date DESC) AS rn
JOIN dim_accounts          AS a ON a.account_id    = u.account_id
JOIN dim_tier_entitlements AS e ON e.contract_tier = a.current_tier
JOIN live                  AS l ON l.account_id    = u.account_id
JOIN sustained AS x ON x.account_id = s.account_id
_notes: LIMIT is a cost control, not an analytical choice. sql/02 returns the whole
ranked book for reporting; the automation only opens deals for the top slice
an AE team can actually work in a day.
months_observed >= 4 mirrors sql/02 exactly, and is load-bearing: without it
the sweep opens deals on accounts whose entire history is the two months of
the breach itself, where there is no trend to speak of - only noise. This
guard is what makes the result set a true subset of sql/02.
Only seat overage is returned. The rate card in data/pricing_rules.json sells
seats and nothing else, so an account over its API or storage pool is a
conversation for sql/02's report, not an auto-created deal with a number on it.

modules.label: Fetch ALL open expansion deals (one call)
_rationale: Suppression stops the sweep re-opening the same deal every morning until
someone closes it, and it checks HubSpot rather than a local table so a deal
a rep created by hand also counts as in-flight.
The obvious implementation - search HubSpot once per candidate - is an N+1.
At LIMIT 25 that is 25 operations per run, 550 a month, which together with
Scenario 1 exceeds the entire free-tier allowance. Fetching the open-deal set
in a single call and matching in memory costs 1 operation instead of 25.
The open expansion pipeline is far below the 100-record page size; if it ever
approaches it, paginate here rather than reverting to per-candidate search.

modules.label: No open expansion deal exists
modules._note: Filters do not consume a Make operation, so the whole suppression step costs 2 operations per run regardless of how many candidates it screens.

modules.label: Open the expansion deal
_notes: Created at qualifiedtobuy, not appointmentscheduled: usage evidence is a
stronger qualification signal than a booked meeting, and the stage drives
the 0.4 forecast weight that reaches Weighted Pipeline Forecast in Power BI.
pricing_variant is 'not_in_test'. Auto-generated expansion deals were never
part of the FY26-H1 randomisation, and letting them inherit an arm would
quietly contaminate sql/01.

operations_budget._method: Make bills one operation per module execution. Filters and routers are free. Modules 1-4 run once per scenario run; modules 6-7 run once per account that clears suppression.

_note: Make's free tier allows 1,000 operations a month. This is the binding constraint
on the whole design and every scheduling decision above traces back to it.
The figure below is what makes the cadences defensible. An earlier draft polled
HubSpot once per candidate for duplicate suppression; that single N+1 pushed the
total to roughly 1,270 and would have silently stalled both scenarios partway
through the month.
operations_budget_total.first_lever_if_exceeded: Drop Scenario 1 polling from hourly to every two hours (-132 operations). Widening the sweep's LIMIT costs nothing, because suppression is batched.

pricing_exceptions.purpose: Standing evidence for the discount-governance review. Deals appear here when they breach the margin floor, exceed a 20% discount, or sit more than 35% off the rate card.

expansion_pipeline.purpose: The AE worklist, and the audit trail proving an auto-created deal came from sustained usage rather than a hunch.

error_handling.policy: Every write module carries an error handler. Silent failure in a pipeline that feeds pricing decisions is worse than a loud stop.

routes.name: unknown_account
routes.action: Log to pricing_exceptions with reason 'unknown_account'; do not insert. The FK on fact_transactions.account_id would reject it regardless.

routes.name: constraint_violation
routes.action: Store the bundle for manual replay and log the constraint name. A 23514 names the CHECK that fired, which points straight at the offending field.

routes.name: neon_cold_start
routes.trigger: connection timeout on first query after idle
routes._note: Neon scales compute to zero. The first query after idle can exceed a default timeout; the second reliably succeeds.

idempotency: Scenario 1 is idempotent through ON CONFLICT (deal_id). Replaying a bundle updates the row rather than duplicating it.
Scenario 2 is idempotent through the module 3 suppression search, not through the database - it creates CRM objects, which have no natural key to conflict on.

security.credentials: Bound in the Make UI only. No token, connection ID or spreadsheet ID appears in this repository.
security.sql_injection: All warehouse writes use positional binding. Deal names are free text and, in any org accepting inbound leads, attacker-controlled.
least_privilege: The Neon role used by Make needs SELECT on dim_accounts, dim_tier_entitlements and
fact_usage_metrics, plus INSERT and UPDATE on fact_transactions. It needs no DDL
CREATE ROLE revyield_automation LOGIN PASSWORD '<managed by Neon>';
GRANT SELECT ON dim_accounts, dim_tier_entitlements, fact_usage_metrics TO revyield_automation;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON fact_transactions TO revyield_automation;
GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCE fact_transactions_transaction_id_seq TO revyield_automation;
security.pii: Company names and deal values only. No personal data leaves HubSpot, so the Google Sheets logs stay outside GDPR personal-data scope.

known_limitations: Polling, not push. A deal edited at 09:05 is priced at 10:00. Real-time write-back needs HubSpot webhooks, which need a paid tier or a public developer app.

Scenario 1 writes straight into fact_transactions. At this volume the constraints are sufficient protection, but a warehouse taking feeds from more than one system should land raw first and transform on the way in.

The company-name join in module 3 is a string match. It holds because dim_accounts.company_name is UNIQUE and is generated, not typed; a real deployment stores the HubSpot company ID on dim_accounts and joins on that.

Suppression in Scenario 2 matches on dealname CONTAINS_TOKEN. Two companies with overlapping names could suppress each other; keying on the associated company ID is the correct fix once HubSpot IDs are stored.
